name: Keswick Hall
positioning: Historic country-house resort, built in 1912, in the Blue Ridge Mountains about 15 minutes from Charlottesville, Virginia, with a Pete Dye golf course
best_for: Golfers who want to stay on the course
Couples looking for a countryside spa getaway

facts.text: The resort sits amid the Blue Ridge Mountains.
Keswick Hall is about 15 minutes from Charlottesville, home to the University of Virginia.
The house was built for the Crawford family in 1912.
The property's former lives include a country club, an Orient-Express hotel and the home of Sir Bernard Ashley, husband and business partner of designer Laura Ashley.
Original fireplaces were restored where possible, as were the intricate millwork and crown molding.
Rooms and suites are adorned in light woods, timeless furnishings and locally inspired photography, with Duxiana mattresses and Red Flower bathroom amenities.
The minibar in each room includes complimentary snacks and drinks.
The spa sits at the edge of woodland, with soft interior lighting and natural finishes.
The spa's serenity room offers weighted blankets, guided meditation tools and freshly steeped herbal teas.
The spa's treatment rooms accommodate couples' services, massages, body treatments and facials, and hair and nail services are offered in its salon.
A natural amphitheater and outdoor-tented area can host up to 400 guests, and indoors a classic ballroom is wrapped in windows.
Crawford's is the all-day restaurant and bar, named after the building's original owners.

highlights.text: The resort has an infinity pool.
Keswick Hall has an 18-hole golf course, Full Cry, by Pete Dye.
Many rooms have private terraces that overlook the golf course.
A percentage of each night's stay goes toward the Thomas Jefferson Foundation.
Marigold by Jean-Georges changes its menu often to offer seasonal produce, much of it grown at the resort's own nearby farm.

considerations.text: Room layouts and furniture differ a great deal, so guests who want a desk or a walk-in closet should request it when booking.
WhataHotel notes the rural location means a car is needed to reach nearby attractions.
